name: NHS & respiratory
summary: UKHSA surveillance shows flu in England above baseline and rising early; week 48 report published 26 Nov
state: UKHSA's weekly flu and COVID-19 surveillance from early November shows influenza activity and hospital admissions in England rising from an early start to the season (UKHSA, week 45). Its week 48 report, with data to 22 Nov, was scheduled for 26 Nov and its figures were not reviewed in this run (UKHSA). Flu is above baseline but not found at high levels nationally, and searches on 26 Nov found no widespread NHS critical incidents, so Watch holds.
for_you: Eligible people can book flu and COVID-19 vaccines through the NHS; use NHS 111 for urgent advice and stay home when unwell.
rubric_hit: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising = Watch; not high nationally
basis_detail: UKHSA surveillance and NHS England situation reports

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
